When corticosteroids are administered concomitantly with potassium-depleting agents (e.g., amphotericin B, diuretics), patients should be observed closely for development of hypokalemia.

warfarin.t: Coadministration of corticosteroids and warfarin usually results in inhibition of response to warfarin, although there have been some conflicting reports.

glucose.t: Because corticosteroids may increase blood glucose concentrations, dosage adjustments of antidiabetic agents may be required.

isoniazid.t: Serum concentrations of isoniazid may be decreased.

aspirin.t: Concomitant use of aspirin (or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents) and corticosteroids increases the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.
Aspirin should be used cautiously in conjunction with corticosteroids in hypoprothrombinemia.

cortico.t: Intramuscular corticosteroid preparations are contraindicated for idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura.
High doses of systemic corticosteroids, including SOLU-CORTEF, should not be used for the treatment of traumatic brain injury.

anticoag.t: Therefore, coagulation indices should be monitored frequently to maintain the desired anticoagulant effect.
